stimulus.title: Making methanol from CO and H₂
stimulus.text: Methanol is made by the reaction CO(g) + 2 H2(g) ⇌ CH3OH(g), ΔH° = −91 kJ/molrxn. At 500 K, Kp = 2.5 × 10−3. A reactor at 500 K contains CO at 2.0 atm, H2 at 4.0 atm and CH3OH at 0.20 atm.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Calculate Qp for the mixture in the reactor.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Determine whether the partial pressure of CH3OH will increase, decrease or stay the same as the mixture approaches equilibrium. Justify your answer.

rubric.point: Decreases: Q<sub>p</sub> (≈ 6.3 × 10⁻³) > K<sub>p</sub> (2.5 × 10⁻³), so the net reaction proceeds in reverse, consuming CH₃OH.

parts.sample: It decreases. Q<sub>p</sub> = 6.3 × 10<sup>−3</sup> is greater than K<sub>p</sub> = 2.5 × 10<sup>−3</sup>, so the net reaction proceeds in reverse, converting CH<sub>3</sub>OH into CO and H<sub>2</sub> until Q<sub>p</sub> = K<sub>p</sub>.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Once the reactor is at equilibrium, its volume is decreased at constant temperature. Explain, in terms of Q and K, why the amount of CH3OH increases.

rubric.point: Decreasing the volume raises every partial pressure by the same factor; because the denominator has P_H₂² × P_CO (three pressure factors) and the numerator one, Q decreases below K, so the net reaction goes forward, forming CH₃OH.
accept: Q falls below K because there are more gas moles on the reactant side
if each pressure doubles, Q becomes Q/4 < K

parts.sample: If the volume is halved, every partial pressure doubles, so Q<sub>p</sub> becomes (2)/((2)(2)<sup>2</sup>) = ¼ of its equilibrium value. Q<sub>p</sub> is then less than K<sub>p</sub>, so the net reaction proceeds forward, forming CH<sub>3</sub>OH until Q<sub>p</sub> = K<sub>p</sub>.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: The temperature of the equilibrium mixture is raised to 550 K. Predict whether Kp at 550 K is greater than, less than or equal to 2.5 × 10−3, and justify your prediction.

rubric.point: Less than: the forward reaction is exothermic (ΔH° < 0), so raising the temperature favors the reverse reaction and K decreases.
accept: K decreases because heat is a product of the forward reaction

parts.sample: Less than 2.5 × 10<sup>−3</sup>. The forward reaction is exothermic (ΔH° = −91 kJ/mol<sub>rxn</sub>), so heat acts as a product; raising the temperature favors the reverse reaction, which means K<sub>p</sub> becomes smaller.
